name: Alexandria Corniche
summary: A long seafront promenade where the city meets the Mediterranean.
description: The Corniche is Alexandria's front porch. Families, fishermen and couples all end up here sooner or later, looking at the same sea. It is less a sight than a habit, which is exactly why it suits a nostalgic mood.
reasonsToVisit: Walk the waterfront as the light turns golden
Stop at a seaside café for tea or coffee
Use it as an easy base for Alexandria's other landmarks
visitorTips: Evenings are the most pleasant time to stroll
Pair it with a visit to Qaitbay Citadel nearby

name: Qaitbay Citadel
summary: A 15th-century fortress at the edge of the harbour.
description: Built by Sultan Qaitbay, the citadel guards the harbour entrance on ground traditionally linked to the ancient Pharos lighthouse. From its walls you can look back at the whole curve of the bay.
reasonsToVisit: Explore a medieval sea fortress
See the harbour and the city skyline from the walls
Watch fishing boats come and go
visitorTips: Bring sun protection; there is little shade on the walls
Check current opening hours locally before you go

name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
summary: A modern library that honours the ancient Library of Alexandria.
description: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina was created to revive the spirit of the ancient Library. The building itself, with its tilted disc roof facing the sea, is worth the visit even if you never open a book.
reasonsToVisit: See striking contemporary architecture by the sea
Visit the reading hall and exhibitions
A thoughtful stop for book lovers
visitorTips: Check current visiting rules and ticketing locally
Allow time to see more than the main hall

name: Montaza Palace Gardens
summary: Royal palace grounds with gardens and sea views.
description: On the eastern side of the city, the Montaza grounds are a leafy retreat of palms, lawns and cliffs above the water. It feels like a postcard from an older, slower Alexandria.
reasonsToVisit: Walk through shaded gardens above the sea
Enjoy views over the water
A relaxed picnic-style outing
visitorTips: The palace building itself may not be open to visitors, so check locally
Go on a clear day for the best sea views

images.alt: Montaza Palace Gardens in Alexandria, Egypt
Another view of Montaza Palace Gardens

name: Siwa Oasis
summary: A remote oasis of palms, salt lakes and mud-brick ruins.
description: Siwa sits far out in the Western Desert, closer to Libya than to Cairo. Its identity is distinct: its own Amazigh language, its own architecture, its own pace. It rewards anyone willing to make the long journey.
reasonsToVisit: Float or wade in the salt lakes
Explore the old mud-brick fortress town of Shali
Visit the ruins linked to the ancient Oracle of Amun
visitorTips: Plan for a long trip from the main cities
Cooler months are generally more comfortable for exploring

name: White Desert National Park
summary: Chalk rock formations carved by wind into surreal shapes.
description: Out past Farafra, the desert floor is dotted with pale chalk sculptures that look like mushrooms, icebergs and animals. Camping here under the stars is the classic way to experience it.
reasonsToVisit: See wind-sculpted chalk formations
Camp overnight in the desert
Watch the colours change from sunset to sunrise
visitorTips: Go with an experienced local operator, not alone
Nights can be cold, so pack warm layers

name: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's Monastery
summary: A mountain pilgrimage and one of the world's oldest working monasteries.
description: Mount Sinai is a place of pilgrimage for several faiths. Many visitors climb in the dark to reach the summit for sunrise, then visit Saint Catherine's Monastery at the foot of the mountain.
reasonsToVisit: Hike to the summit for sunrise
Visit Saint Catherine's Monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Experience the rugged granite landscape of South Sinai
visitorTips: Bring a headlamp and warm clothing for the night climb
Check monastery visiting times before you travel
mapQuery: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's Monastery, South Sinai, Egypt

Another view of Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's Monastery

name: Wadi El Hitan (Valley of the Whales)
summary: A desert valley of fossilised early whales, listed by UNESCO.
description: Millions of years ago this dry valley was under water. Today you can walk a marked trail among the skeletons of early whales lying in the sand, a rare chance to see evolution laid out in the open air.
reasonsToVisit: Walk among fossilised whale skeletons
See a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Pair it with other desert stops in the Faiyum
visitorTips: Bring water and sun protection
A local guide or driver is useful for the desert tracks
mapQuery: Wadi El Hitan (Valley of the Whales), Faiyum, Egypt

name: Philae Temple
summary: A temple of Isis on an island, reached by boat.
description: Philae was moved stone by stone to a new island when the old one was flooded by the Aswan dams. Arriving by boat across still water, with the temple rising ahead, is one of the most atmospheric entrances in Egypt.
reasonsToVisit: Take a short boat ride to the island
Admire the temple dedicated to Isis
Visit in soft evening or morning light
visitorTips: Boat transfers are part of the visit; confirm arrangements locally
Check whether the evening sound-and-light show is running

name: Elephantine Island
summary: A quiet Nile island with ruins and Nubian villages.
description: In the middle of the river at Aswan, Elephantine feels like a small, separate world. Narrow lanes, colourful houses and the sound of water make it ideal for a long, unhurried walk together.
reasonsToVisit: Wander through Nubian village lanes
See ancient ruins on the island
Take a felucca around the island at sunset
visitorTips: Reach it by a short boat ride from the Aswan waterfront
Respect local customs when photographing residents

name: Luxor Temple
summary: A temple in the middle of the city, glowing at night.
description: Unlike most ancient sites, Luxor Temple sits right in the town, beside the Nile corniche. After dark, when the columns are lit, it becomes one of the most beautiful evening walks in Egypt.
reasonsToVisit: See the temple lit up after dark
Walk the Nile corniche beside it
Combine it with a sunset felucca ride
visitorTips: Evening visits are especially atmospheric
Check current opening hours locally

name: Dahab
summary: A laid-back Red Sea town between mountains and water.
description: Dahab moves slowly. Cafés line the waterfront, the mountains sit behind, and the sea is right there. It is known for snorkelling and diving, but doing nothing very well is also a perfectly good plan.
reasonsToVisit: Sit by the water with a book
Snorkel or dive in clear Red Sea water
Take a quiet walk along the bay
visitorTips: Water conditions vary, so ask local operators about safety
Spring and autumn are often pleasant

name: Wadi El Rayan Protected Area
summary: Lakes, waterfalls and dunes within a short drive of Cairo.
description: A surprising mix of desert and water: lakes ringed with sand dunes, plus one of Egypt's few natural-looking waterfalls. It is peaceful, open and easy to reach for a day trip.
reasonsToVisit: Sit by the lakes and watch the dunes
See the waterfalls
Easy day trip for a quiet reset
visitorTips: Bring your own water and snacks
Go early to avoid weekend crowds

name: Lake Qarun
summary: A large inland lake framed by desert and farmland.
description: Lake Qarun is one of the oldest lakes in the world, and its shores are a good spot for birdwatching and slow lakeside afternoons. Nearby villages add pottery, cafés and easy walks.
reasonsToVisit: Watch birds along the shore
Enjoy a slow lakeside afternoon
Combine with a day in the Faiyum villages
visitorTips: Check seasons if birdwatching is your goal
A local driver makes the Faiyum easier to explore
